level.basicHint: Short, simple exchanges. Key words and sentence starters help you along.
level.intermediateHint: Everyday topics in a few sentences. Feedback on frequent patterns.
level.advancedHint: Opinions, nuance and debate. Feedback on register and naturalness.
focusMode.freeHint: Talk about anything around the topic.
focusMode.pendingHint: Your partner steers towards what you're working on, without saying so.
drillFormat.transformationHint: Rewrite a sentence into the target form.
drillFormat.guidedChatHint: A short chat where the structure comes naturally.
drillFormat.spotErrorHint: Find the sentence with the slip, then fix it.

onboarding.nativeLang.title: What's your first language?
onboarding.nativeLang.body: Feedback and explanations will be written in it.
onboarding.nativeLang.required: Choose your first language to continue.
onboarding.name.title: What should we call you?

onboarding.goal.title: What do you want English for?

onboarding.interests.title: What do you like talking about?

onboarding.connection.required: Save an API key or find Claude Code to continue.

onboarding.variant.title: Which English would you like?
onboarding.variant.body: Your partner will spell and choose words this way.
onboarding.reminder.title: A daily reminder?
onboarding.reminder.body: One quiet notification at this time. Missing a day never breaks anything.
onboarding.level.title: Where would you like to start?
onboarding.level.body: You can change it before any conversation.
connection.apiKeyBody: Kept in your system keychain and sent only to Anthropic.

connection.modelHint: One model for conversation, feedback and practice.
connection.modelsWaiting: Connect first to see the models you can use.
connection.effortHint: More effort means more careful answers, but slower and more expensive.

spelling.strictBody: Accents have to be right too.
readAloud.body: A voice on this computer reads the English on the screen: your partner's lines and the words you practise. Nothing leaves it.

setup.topicRequired: Write a topic or pick a suggestion.
setup.targetHint: Minutes you spend speaking or writing, not time on screen.
setup.materialPlaceholder: Paste an article, an email, anything you'd like to talk about.

conversation.label: Conversation
conversation.encourage1: Keep going — say it however you can. We'll fix things at the end.
conversation.encourage3: Rough is fine. Ideas first, polish later.
conversation.encourage4: Say it your way. The feedback waits until the end.

conversation.micHold: Microphone. Hold to talk, or press to start and stop. Shortcut: Ctrl+Space.

conversation.helpEmpty: Nothing came back. Try other words.

analysis.note: Only a few things come back: the ones worth your time.

report.keys: Use the arrow keys to move between cards.
report.empty: Too little to go on this time. Talk a bit longer and the feedback will have something to say.
report.achievement.title: What went well
report.focus.title: One thing to work on
report.correction.notFixed: Not this time. Here it is.
report.couldHaveSaid.title: You could have said

structures.terms.participle.hint: The third form of the verb: built, done, seen.
structures.terms.ing.hint: The verb ending in -ing: reading, working.
structures.terms.past.hint: The second form of the verb: watched, went.
structures.terms.present.hint: The verb as it is, with -s after he, she or it: rain, rains.
structures.terms.verb.hint: The action word, as the dictionary lists it: go, eat.
structures.terms.be.hint: The verb “to be”, in the form the sentence needs: am, is, are, was, were, be.
structures.terms.auxiliary.hint: A helping verb that goes with another: have, do, will.
structures.terms.subject.hint: Who does the action: I, she, the dog.
structures.terms.object.hint: What the action lands on: my hair, the car.
structures.terms.noun.hint: A person, thing or idea: coffee, friend.
structures.terms.adjective.hint: A word that describes: cheap, good.
structures.catalogue.present-simple.form: subject + verb (+ s with he, she, it)
structures.catalogue.present-simple.use: Habits and facts. With he, she or it the verb takes an -s.
structures.catalogue.present-simple.goal: Say something someone always does, or a fact.
structures.catalogue.present-simple.samp: Her daily habit: going to work on foot.
Something happening now, or around now.
Say something going on right now, or these days.
These days: me, in the middle of a great book.
structures.catalogue.past-simple.form: verb in the past (-ed or irregular)
structures.catalogue.past-simple.use: A finished action at a past time.
structures.catalogue.past-simple.goal: Say something that is over, at a past time.
structures.catalogue.past-simple.sample: Last night, a film: over and done.
structures.catalogue.was-were.form: was / were + adjective, noun or place
structures.catalogue.was-were.use: How something or someone was. Was with I, he, she, it; were with the rest.
structures.catalogue.was-were.goal: Say how something or someone was, back then.
structures.catalogue.was-were.sample: The food, back then: really good.
structures.catalogue.going-to.form: am / is / are going to + verb
structures.catalogue.going-to.use: Plans already decided. The verb stays in its base form.
structures.catalogue.going-to.goal: Say a plan you have already made.
structures.catalogue.going-to.sample: My plan for tomorrow: a call to her.
structures.catalogue.will.use: Decisions made on the spot, promises and predictions.
structures.catalogue.will.goal: Decide on the spot, promise or predict.
structures.catalogue.will.sample: An offer made on the spot: my help with that.
structures.catalogue.can.use: Ability or possibility. After can, the verb takes no to.
structures.catalogue.can.goal: Say what someone is able to do, or isn't.
structures.catalogue.can.sample: Swimming: not one of my skills.
structures.catalogue.have-to.use: What is necessary. Don't have to means there is no need.
structures.catalogue.have-to.sample: Tomorrow, an early start: no choice.
structures.catalogue.would-like.form: would like + noun, or + to + verb
structures.catalogue.would-like.use: Asking for something, or saying what you want, politely.
structures.catalogue.would-like.goal: Ask for something, or say what you want, politely.
structures.catalogue.would-like.sample: A polite wish: trying that place.
structures.catalogue.there-is.form: there is + singular, there are + plural
structures.catalogue.comparatives.form: adjective-er than, or more + adjective + than
structures.catalogue.comparatives.use: Comparing two things. Short adjectives take -er, long ones take more.
structures.catalogue.comparatives.sample: Two phones: the price of this one against mine.
structures.catalogue.superlatives.form: the + adjective-est, or the most + adjective
structures.catalogue.superlatives.use: The one that stands out in a group.
structures.catalogue.superlatives.goal: Say which one stands out in its group.
structures.catalogue.superlatives.sample: Every pizza in town, and this one on top.
structures.catalogue.present-perfect.use: Experiences or something recent, with no finished time. With a date it is the past simple.
structures.catalogue.present-perfect.goa: Tell an experience or something recent, without saying when.
structures.catalogue.present-perfect.sam: Lisbon: two visits so far, no dates.
structures.catalogue.present-perfect-con: Something that started in the past and still goes on.
Say something that started earlier and still goes on.
This job: two years, and still going.
structures.catalogue.past-continuous.use: An action in progress in the past, often cut short by another.
structures.catalogue.past-continuous.goa: Say what was going on at a moment in the past.
structures.catalogue.past-continuous.sam: Your call came in the middle of my cooking.
structures.catalogue.past-perfect.use: An action that came before another past action.
structures.catalogue.past-perfect.goal: Say something that came before another past event.
structures.catalogue.past-perfect.sample: First she left; only then did I get there.
structures.catalogue.used-to.use: A past habit or state that is no longer true.
structures.catalogue.used-to.goal: Say something that was a habit or true once, and no longer is.
structures.catalogue.used-to.sample: The piano: once a habit of mine, not any more.
structures.catalogue.first-conditional.u: Something possible in the future. After if comes the present, never will.
structures.catalogue.first-conditional.g: Say what comes next if something possible happens.
structures.catalogue.first-conditional.s: Rain is possible; in that case, home for us.
Something imagined or unlikely. After if comes the past; in the other half, would.
Imagine something unreal and say what would follow.
No time, in fact; with it, more trips.
structures.catalogue.passive.use: What happens to something, when who does it matters less.
structures.catalogue.passive.goal: Say what happened to something or someone, not who did it.
structures.catalogue.passive.sample: Somebody built the bridge in 1920; who is left out.
structures.catalogue.relative-clauses.us: Saying which person or thing you mean.
structures.catalogue.relative-clauses.go: Name someone or something and say which one you mean, in one sentence.
structures.catalogue.relative-clauses.sa: A guy lives next door. He is a chef. Both, in one sentence.
structures.catalogue.reported-speech.for: said / told + (that) + clause one tense back
structures.catalogue.reported-speech.use: Telling what someone said: the tense moves one step back.
structures.catalogue.reported-speech.goa: Tell what someone said, without quoting them.
structures.catalogue.reported-speech.sam: His words were “I'm tired”; pass them on.
structures.catalogue.modals-of-deduction: How sure you are: must when certain, might when possible, can't when impossible.
Make a guess and show how sure you are.
No proof, but I'm sure: at this hour, she is at work.
structures.catalogue.verb-patterns.form: verb + verb-ing, or verb + to + verb
structures.catalogue.verb-patterns.use: A verb after another: some take -ing (enjoy, avoid), others to (want, forget).
structures.catalogue.verb-patterns.goal: Use two verbs in a row: the first decides the shape of the second.
structures.catalogue.verb-patterns.sampl: The kitchen: a pleasure. The rice: forgotten at the shop.
structures.catalogue.third-conditional.f: if + had + past participle, would have + past participle
structures.catalogue.third-conditional.u: A past that did not happen, and its imagined result.
structures.catalogue.third-conditional.g: Imagine a different past and what would have followed.
structures.catalogue.third-conditional.s: I didn't know, so I didn't come; imagine the opposite.
structures.catalogue.mixed-conditional.f: if + had + past participle, would + verb
structures.catalogue.mixed-conditional.u: A past that did not happen, and what would be different now.
structures.catalogue.mixed-conditional.g: Imagine a different past and how today would be.
structures.catalogue.mixed-conditional.s: No law degree then, so no lawyer today; imagine the opposite.
structures.catalogue.wish.form: wish + past, or wish + had + past participle
structures.catalogue.wish.use: Regret: wish with the past for now, with had for the past.
structures.catalogue.wish.goal: Regret how something is or was.
structures.catalogue.wish.sample: A regret: too little studying, back then.
structures.catalogue.modal-perfect.form: should / might / must + have + past participle
structures.catalogue.modal-perfect.use: Judging or guessing about the past.
structures.catalogue.modal-perfect.goal: Judge or guess about something already past.
structures.catalogue.modal-perfect.sampl: You didn't tell me, and that was a mistake.
structures.catalogue.future-continuous.u: An action in progress at a moment in the future.
structures.catalogue.future-continuous.g: Say what will be going on at a moment in the future.
structures.catalogue.future-continuous.s: Tomorrow, this same hour: me, mid-flight to Rome.
structures.catalogue.future-perfect.use: Something finished before a moment in the future.
structures.catalogue.future-perfect.goal: Say what will be done before a moment in the future.
structures.catalogue.future-perfect.samp: Friday comes; the work is done before it.
structures.catalogue.causative.use: Something you arrange for someone else to do for you.
structures.catalogue.causative.goal: Say something another person does for you, at your request.
structures.catalogue.causative.sample: Yesterday a hairdresser cut my hair, at my request.
structures.catalogue.passive-reporting.f: it is said that, or subject + is said to + verb
structures.catalogue.passive-reporting.u: What people say or believe, without saying who.
structures.catalogue.passive-reporting.g: Tell what people say or believe, without saying who.
structures.catalogue.passive-reporting.s: People say it of him: the best in the country.
structures.catalogue.cleft.form: what + clause + is, or it is / was + focus + that
structures.catalogue.cleft.use: Putting the weight on one part of the sentence.
structures.catalogue.cleft.goal: Make one part of the sentence stand out.
structures.catalogue.cleft.sample: I need a long holiday, with all the weight on the holiday.
structures.catalogue.inversion.form: never / hardly / not only + auxiliary + subject
structures.catalogue.inversion.use: Emphasis: after never or hardly, the auxiliary goes before the subject.
structures.catalogue.inversion.goal: Say something with strong emphasis, in a formal way.
structures.catalogue.inversion.sample: I have never seen such a mess, said with force.
verb-ing or past participle clause + main clause
Joining two actions of the same subject in one sentence.
Join two actions by the same person in one sentence.
I walked home. On the way, I ran into an old friend.
structures.catalogue.would-rather.form: would rather + verb, or would rather + subject + past
structures.catalogue.would-rather.use: What you prefer, for yourself or from someone else.
structures.catalogue.would-rather.goal: Say what you prefer, for yourself or from someone else.
structures.catalogue.would-rather.sample: My preference: this stays between us.

listening.paused.title: Paused

listening.reading.hidden: The text is hidden. Just listen.

listening.run.retry: You missed this one before. Here it is again.
listening.run.why.slowed: You slowed it down after hearing it: it counts at the slower pace.
listening.run.why.listens: It took more than two listens.

listening.summary.notYet: No pace is yours yet: keep going.
listening.summary.hint.faster: Two dictations understood at this pace. Try a faster one.
listening.summary.hint.slower: This one was hard. A slower pace will help you tell the words apart.
